title: Grade 5 Science — Mon, May 18
description: Living Things & Cells — Last Week Day 1
subject: science

questions.question: What is the basic unit of life?
questions.explanation: The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of all living things.

questions.question: Who discovered the cell?
questions.explanation: Robert Hooke discovered the cell in 1665 while examining cork under a microscope.

questions.question: Which cell organelle controls the cell's activities?
questions.explanation: The nucleus is the 'control centre' of the cell — it contains DNA and directs cell activities.

questions.question: Which is present in plant cells but NOT in animal cells?
questions.explanation: Plant cells have a rigid cell wall made of cellulose. Animal cells do not have a cell wall.

questions.question: What does the mitochondria do?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria are called the 'powerhouse of the cell' because they produce energy through respiration.

questions.question: Unicellular organisms consist of:
questions.explanation: Unicellular means single-celled. Examples: Amoeba, paramecium, bacteria.

questions.question: Which is an example of a unicellular organism?
questions.explanation: Amoeba is a unicellular organism — its entire body is a single cell.

questions.question: The green pigment in plant cells that helps in photosynthesis is:
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll in chloroplasts absorbs sunlight for photosynthesis.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a characteristic of living things?
questions.explanation: Rusting is a chemical reaction in non-living iron. Living things grow, reproduce, and respire.

questions.question: Blood cells are produced in:
questions.explanation: Red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets are produced in bone marrow.

questions.question: Which part of the cell controls what enters and exits?
questions.explanation: The cell membrane is selectively permeable — it controls which substances enter and exit the cell.

questions.question: A group of similar cells performing the same function is called a:
questions.explanation: Tissue is a group of similar cells working together. Multiple tissues form organs.

questions.question: The nerve cell is also called:
questions.explanation: Nerve cells are called neurons. They transmit electrical signals in the nervous system.

questions.question: Which organism reproduces by binary fission?
questions.explanation: Bacteria reproduce asexually by binary fission — one cell splits into two identical cells.

questions.question: Chloroplasts are found in plant cells because plants:
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll needed for photosynthesis — making food from sunlight.
